title: Define backup compatibility guarantees + migration strategy (Private backup/restore)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
We need a clear, documented compatibility policy between (a) Redwood Private platform versions, (b) private-installer versions, and (c) backup artifact format versions. This includes: (1) a compatibility matrix that Support/SE can reference, (2) enforcement behavior in tooling (restore should refuse/guide on incompatible combos), and (3) a migration strategy for old backup artifacts so restores remain deterministic across upgrades.

This work unblocks enterprise commitments for DR readiness (FinBank, MedData) and reduces restore drill failures due to format drift/CRD ordering issues.
acceptance_criteria:
- Publish a compatibility policy with explicit guarantees:
  - backward compatibility window (how far back we support restoring from)
  - forward compatibility stance (whether a newer backup can be restored by an older installer)
  - what constitutes a breaking change
- Produce an operator-facing compatibility matrix (doc + versioned artifact in repo) covering:
  - Platform version (redwood-private control plane)
  - private-installer version
  - backup format version
  - required migration steps (if any)
- Implement restore-time checks (installer) that:
  - read backup manifest metadata
  - verify format version + platform version constraints
  - fail fast with actionable error messages and links to docs
- Define and implement migration tooling strategy:
  - either `backup migrate` (offline-capable) OR a library invoked automatically during restore
  - deterministic output + integrity verification
- Document how migrations behave in air-gapped installs (no external fetches) and how to stage migrations safely
- Add test cases in restore validation plan for:
  - restoring backups created from N-2 and N-1 platform versions
  - attempting restore with incompatible installer versions
  - migration success + checksum verification
- Review with Security (encryption + key handling unchanged by migration) and Release Eng (bundle versioning rules)
proposed_approach:
Policy proposal (draft):
- Backup artifacts are versioned with `backup_format_version` (semver) stored in a human-readable manifest.
- We guarantee:
  1) Backward restore compatibility: installer version X can restore backups created by platform versions within the last 2 minor releases (N-2) as long as the backup format major version matches.
  2) Forward restore compatibility: not guaranteed (older installer restoring a newer backup should be blocked).
  3) Breaking changes only occur on backup format MAJOR bumps and require a migration step.

Tooling:
- `restore apply` reads the manifest, validates:
  - `backup_format_version` major equals supported major
  - backup producer platform version is within supported window
  - required components are present (manifest entries)
- If migration required:
  - Prefer explicit `backup migrate --in <artifact> --out <artifact>` for clarity and air-gapped workflows
  - Restore can also offer `--auto-migrate` as a convenience in non-regulated environments (default off for now)

Where the matrix lives:
- Source-of-truth: docs + versioned CSV/MD in installer repo so it can ship in offline bundle.
- Also mirrored into Confluence runbook for internal operations + Support.
compatibility_matrix_draft:
Draft matrix (subject to finalization):

Definitions:
- Platform version = control-plane release running when backup was created
- Installer version = private-installer used for restore
- Format version = manifest field `backup_format_version`

| Backup producer platform | Backup format | Restore installer | Supported? | Action |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| 2025.01 (N-2) | 1.0.x | 2025.03 | Yes | Restore directly |
| 2025.02 (N-1) | 1.0.x | 2025.03 | Yes | Restore directly |
| 2025.03 (N) | 1.1.x | 2025.03 | Yes | Restore directly |
| 2025.03 (N) | 1.1.x | 2025.02 | No | Upgrade installer |
| <= 2024.12 | 0.x | 2025.03 | No (by default) | Escalate to Support; migration not provided |

Breaking scenario examples:
- Major bump 1.x -> 2.x: restore must block unless `backup migrate` is run.

Notes:
- If platform/CRDs changed (e.g., new required CRD for restore ordering), compatibility is controlled by installer + chart version alignment; matrix must call out required minimum chart versions.
open_questions:
- What is the official version identifier for the Private platform in customer-facing docs (calendar version vs internal git SHA)? Proposal: use a calendar release tag (YYYY.MM) and include git SHA in manifest for debugging.
- How strict should the restore window be (N-2 vs N-3) for large enterprise upgrade cycles?
- Should we treat changes in included/excluded resource sets as breaking? (e.g., new mandatory config store)
- Who owns updating the matrix each release: Release Eng gate vs Control Plane team? Proposal: release checklist requires updating matrix + tests.
- Do we need per-deployment-type exceptions (VPC vs on-prem) if k8s minor versions differ materially?
implementation_notes:
Manifest fields (proposed minimum):
- backup_id (uuid)
- created_at (RFC3339)
- backup_format_version (semver)
- producer:
  - platform_version (YYYY.MM)
  - platform_git_sha
  - installer_version (if invoked via installer)
- encryption:
  - scheme (envelope)
  - kms_provider (aws-kms | gcp-kms | local-gpg | hsm)
  - key_id (redacted/partial)
- components:
  - config_db snapshot info
  - control-plane config export
  - k8s/helm metadata (release names, namespace)
- integrity:
  - sha256 checksums per artifact

Migration contract:
- Migrations must not decrypt plaintext onto disk unless explicitly requested; default should stream decrypt->transform->encrypt.
- Output artifact must have new manifest + new checksums; must preserve a link to input artifact id.
- Migration must be deterministic and offline-capable (no fetching schemas from the internet).

comments: 2025-02-18 — Talia Benson (PM): Creating this ticket after DR rehearsal feedback. We need something Support can point at that clearly states what we support, and tooling that enforces it (no more “it might work”).

2025-02-19 — Sean Gallagher (SRE): +1. Restore drill failure last week was partly due to chart/CRD mismatch. Whatever matrix we publish needs to include the k8s/Helm expectations (or at least call out that restore requires installer bundle for same release train). Also: restore should fail fast before doing anything destructive.

2025-02-21 — Michael Nguyen (Assignee): Drafting policy: no forward-compat; backward support N-2 minor releases; breaking changes only on backup format major. Will propose manifest fields + error codes so Support can triage quickly. Next step: align with Connor/Sahana on release gating (matrix update required).

2025-02-24 — Hanae Suzuki (Security): Migration must not weaken encryption posture. If migrate requires decrypting, it needs to be streaming and re-encrypt with customer-managed key. Also make sure key identifiers are not logged in full in manifest/logs; we can include last 4 or a hash for correlation.

2025-03-03 — Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): We can add a release gate: (1) compatibility matrix file updated for the release, (2) restore validation tests run for N-1 backup, (3) offline bundle includes matrix + docs snapshot. Please make sure the matrix lives in the installer repo so it ships to air-gapped customers.

2025-03-07 — Michael Nguyen (Assignee): Implementing restore-time checks behind feature flag `RESTORE_COMPAT_CHECKS=1` in staging first. Planning to land in installer 2025.03 with default ON. Will follow up with Elliot/Kira to ensure docs mention “installer must be >= backup producer installer” and include upgrade guidance.
